rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words — grep zero-tolerance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: view greps em_dash 0, banned_words 0, leverage_verb 0 (all CLEAN, planted-proof). Harm (consultancy register, hook-bypassed em-dash) absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Ritual / ceremony — hard ban
rules_evaluated.evidence: view grep ritual_ceremony 0 CLEAN; grep -nEi '\bpractice' over body -> 0. Harm (ritual register) absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
rules_evaluated.evidence: view greps dated_line 0, session_biography 0 (CLEAN). Maintainer tense test: closest L85 'personal-agent-homework-3 unchanged, for a run that did not fire' states the reuse fact as it stands now, not an edit; L87 'Nothing before the rerun names what kind of line it was' is present state. No transition verb narrating an edit. Harm (changelog in a block) absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Register match.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Voice: warm, concrete, peer register. Closest L72 'That is a team call, not a vote, and nobody's agent makes it.' is a flat factual boundary, not poster register. Retain-this grep (Remember|Hold onto|Keep in mind|Never forget) over body -> 0. Atmospheric closest L51 'Laptops half shut.' is a plain posture cue, no sensory/isolation imagery. No negation-callout contradicted in-paragraph.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Credit original when paraphrasing named technique.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -nE 'Antti|the creator|the author' body -> 0; view author_we 0 CLEAN; grep -nE '^\s*(We|we)\b' body -> 0. Closest L17 'the trainer's fallback digest': sanctioned 'the trainer' where the student needs to know who holds a rescue. No named technique paraphrased without credit (asking for the reverse of your own line is generic). Maintainer L96 '(workshop §11)' is a numbered compendium pointer; the sub-rule is a soft switch-to-name candidate and existing numbered references stay.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Always "you", never "the student"; teacher framing stays out of body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: view grep the_student 0 CLEAN. Closest L17 'takes the trainer's fallback digest': names who holds a rescue the student needs, not delivery choreography ('the trainer shows...').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle terms of art from maintainer into body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest terms 'the door' L21/L33 and 'look-for line' L33/L51. Both earned upstream: apt101-send-it-off L55 'For the boundary, the door: the digest reads only your memory, and only what the team let in.' and the Day 1 look-for line is authored in morning.md per the Consumes list. No maintainer-only term (self-compound, substrate, grill-me) in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Over-hedge detector.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -nEi 'no penalty|fine way to|it.s OK if|consolation|not a downgrade|on the hook|box-check' over body -> 0. Closest L45 'If your doubt lands on a typo, look again.' is a redirect with a reason, not an absolution.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Punchy framing keeps punch; carve-out lives downstream.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest punchy line L76 'The digest read more than any of you could.' The next sentence ('Each of you still knew one source well enough to catch where it went past what was there.') supplies the boundary in concrete terms one sentence downstream, which is the rule's shape.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Value-prop / positioning framing belongs in sales copy + project strategy docs, NOT student-facing curriculum body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -nEi 'vendor|not theoretical|grounded in actual|this isn.t marketing|unlike consultancy' over body -> 0. No positioning posture inside a teaching beat.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Watch out for planting jargon too early.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest L21/L33 'hypothesis' (fence), 'brief', 'door': each earned by Day 1 exercises. grep -nEi 'token|embedding|retrieval|inference|fine-tun|orchestrat|schema|frontmatter' over body -> 0. Operational copy (phase headers, lead-ins) uses plain words at this arc position.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audit closer when trimming body-prose forcing function.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest closers: L45 'If your doubt lands on a typo, look again.' (object = the doubt just picked) and L76 'catch where it went past what was there' ('it' = the digest, single referent). No post-trim bypass punchline ('go fix it').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The `**What happened:**` block is OPTIONAL — default is to omit it (Antti-directed 2026-08-12, mandation removed from `curriculum/exercises/README.md`).
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -c '\*\*What happened:\*\*' over body -> 0. Block omitted, the rule's default. '## Take stock' L74-76 names artifacts held, not a replay of steps.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -nEiw 'bark|order|command|whip|force|drag|boss|shout|snap|lecture|scold' over body -> 0. Closest L31 'Push back if the list comes back as a summary' is peer-flat corpus idiom.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Headers L23 'See what ran', L35 'Mark the line you trust least', L47 'Read your lines aloud', L56 'Ask it the other way round', L66 'Pick the doubt'. Closest L56: 'it' = Claude, 'the other way round' = the reversed look-for line, which is what Phase 4 does; no 'other X' presupposing a primary, no spatial metaphor contradicting the mechanism.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Machine-cadence fat — the shape of good prose without the content.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest (a) L72 'a team call, not a vote' negates the trio's real prior once; L31 'not a second essay about the first one' negates the actual failure (agent re-summarises); L41 'Not the one that is plainly wrong' separates two real candidates. (b) L72 'That is a team call' characterises the pick rather than pointing at a claim restated in the same clause. (c)/(d) no bold-label echo, no citation block.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L27: 'the two lines you wrote into the brief on Day 1, what to look for and what you expected'. The numeral sits directly against the two-item list it counts and is never reused later as a handle, so it is a second copy of what the list carries. (The 'four lines' L27/L31/L51 and 'two headlines' L64/L76 are reused across phases as the exercise's own handles and fall inside the memory-handle carve-out; not filed.) Harm: a count silently falsified by the next edit to the list. Present here in small form.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Drop the numeral: 'the lines you wrote into the brief on Day 1, what to look for and what you expected'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slogan that is false as stated is not punchy framing — run the truth test before reaching for §12.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L39: 'Every line in it came from your material.' Superlative about how the digest behaves, not an artifact we built. Counterexample from the exercise's own contingency: the Phase 1 fence asks Claude to give each claim 'the source file it came from, or "no source"', the Phase 2 fence says 'If the source doesn't say it, say so plainly', and L76 says the agent 'went past what was there'. Harm (a professional finds the false 'every' faster than the author) is present, and the next sentence 'You know these sources' already carries the weight.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut the superlative: 'The digest is built from your material. You know these sources. The agent read them once.'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A sentence saying how you'd know points at the outcome, not the nearest artifact.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest L45/L76 how-you'd-know clauses point at outcomes: Phase 2 fence has Claude put 'the source's own sentence next to the digest's line, both quoted exactly' (an observation that can come back negative), and L76 'catch where it went past what was there'. No self-witnessing instrument.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Say it once, at its most concrete, then at most one sentence that generalises it. Style, not a gate.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Advisory rule (own text: 'Not a REVISE on its own'). Closest L27 restates parts of the apt101-d2-what-ran-overnight fence below it (class b); the fence is long and multi-step so a fuller lead-in is defensible under check_prompts 2a. L21 'What you do' paragraph previews the phases once; no third sentence on one idea. No superlative, so §21 does not own a sentence here beyond L39 (filed there).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body prose stands without the trainer — no cue-card prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Muted read: every body sentence carries a verb and a page-named subject except verbless L27/L60 'Each of you, on your own laptop.' (names who and where) and L51 'Laptops half shut.' (posture cue; same shape judged fine in apt101-map-the-story L82); the next sentence in each carries a full instruction. Report-only grep Take a guess|before it runs|on the screen|^Let's go|^Go\.|Your turn|What does .* now\? -> 0. Pronouns resolve on the page.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest L39 'You know these sources. The agent read them once.' puts the student as the authority, an aspirational stance. grep -nEi 'beginner|senior|at your scale|more experienced' over body -> 0. Identity-criterion shape ('the difference is whether') -> 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Earn every technical term on first use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest 'Routines list', 'Run now', 'brief', 'door', 'look-for line': introduced in Day 1 exercises or are product UI labels the student used on Day 1. No unearned term; audience is product people who just used each.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Business-audience word ban (Agents 101 default).
rules_evaluated.evidence: SVP test on body terms: 'digest', 'brief', 'headline', 'doubt', 'source' are ordinary working words. No flinch term.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Memory vs context — use deliberately.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -nEi 'memory|context' over body -> 0. The only 'memory/' is inside the reused fence personal-agent-homework-3 ('Read the current state of memory/ as context'), used correctly (memory = folder, context = what it reads).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Golden path only in body — THIS RULE HAS AN EXCEPTION; read to the boundary before cutting anything.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest L13 'If its last run is from before Day 1 ended, click Run now' and L17 'Only a laptop that cannot run the brief at all takes the trainer's fallback digest': plausible failure (a scheduled run that did not fire) with a non-obvious rescue, kept in body next to the risk. Not a pre-emptive FAQ. View-summary line L102 ships and was read as body (see rule 22).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust Claude's defaults for structure.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest apt101-d2-what-ran-overnight specifies shape (four quoted lines, ranked list with sources); the teaching depends on quote-exactly and 'no source'. Phase 4 fence ends with destination and 'Add nothing.'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't ask student to manually diff or spot-check Claude's output as error-catching.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest Phase 2 L39-41: the student picks the line they trust least, but the student is the authority on that criterion ('You know these sources') and the fence has Claude put the source's sentence beside the line. Look-lines name object and tell: L41 'the one you would least want a priority call to rest on'; L53-55 questions name what to compare. No attitude adverb (grep carefully|closely|thoroughly|properly -> 0). L72 'The product owner writes the chosen doubt' names the person, not whether by hand or through Claude; a direct 'you do it' is acceptable under the carve-out. Speech verbs L33 carry an addressee ('to the other two').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No "What research says" callout boxes
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -ni 'What research says' over body -> 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Student moves stay in conversation with agent.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Phases 1, 2, 4 run through Claude; no editor/terminal/file-edit primitive asked. Closest L72 'The product owner writes the chosen doubt at the top of team/doubts.md': a team-file write by a person, not a manual-git or editor primitive as forcing function.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Specify which CLAUDE.md layer — every time.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body prose names no CLAUDE.md (grep CLAUDE -> 0 in body). The only mention is inside the reused fence personal-agent-homework-3: 'the root CLAUDE.md', which names the layer.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No em-dashes. Simple sentences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: view em_dash 0 CLEAN; grep -c '—' over the four fence files -> 0 each. Closest L27: a 45-word second sentence with a list and a coordinate clause. Split by commas into plain clauses, no em-dash sub-clause; offered as a suggestion, not owed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Section headers use command verbs when section is about doing something.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Headers open on a command verb the student owns: 'See', 'Mark', 'Read', 'Ask', 'Pick', 'Take stock'. grep 'Claude' in '^#' lines -> 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Inline links use target's title, never filename.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L13: 'start Phase 1 when `module-2/morning-agent/latest.html` lands'. The rule names 'Phase 3' as a position-class reference; inserting or reordering a phase silently repoints it, and a bare direction serves here. Harm (stale coordinate) is small but the swap costs nothing. 'Day 1'/'Day 2' are the training's fixed schedule names, not positions inside this file; not filed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguate shared-word collisions with Claude Code primitives on first student-authored use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: First student-authored write of a contested word: none; no memory/skill/rule file is authored (doubts.md is a plain notes file). grep -nEiw 'here|above|below' over body -> 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: LLM-vs-agent-vs-Claude vocabulary discipline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Claude for plain service asks (L27 'Ask Claude to keep a copy...', L41, L60 'Ask Claude to run your digest once more...'); 'the agent' for the acting system (L21 'Each of your agents ran overnight', L39, L72 'nobody's agent'). Not assistant-shaped framing. Closest L60 'run your digest once more' is an execution but a plain service ask, no self-critique stance.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Session / task / run split (all trainings).
rules_evaluated.evidence: 'run' as noun for the completed delegated execution read from outside (L27 'tonight's run overwrites them', L33 'If the run read any file outside...'), UI label ('Run now'), and verb. No noun-run for the agent sitting; 'session' used for the sitting (L7, L13).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No time-of-day anchors in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule question, not filed. grep -nEi 'tomorrow|overnight|tonight|this morning|yesterday|last night' over body -> L13 (routine name 'Overnight digest'), L21 'ran overnight', L27 'tonight's run' and 'what ran overnight' (the latter is part of the registry key name only), plus L102 'your overnight agent' in the shipped view summary. Harm the rule prevents (a module pinned to a gap that varies by cohort cadence) is absent in substance: the training is a fixed Day 1 -> Day 2 sequence whose spine is the overnight digest, and L13 already handles a non-overnight gap ('If its last run is from before Day 1 ended, click Run now'). Same call sibling apt101 files received. What the rule would have to say: carve out fixed-cadence trainings whose artifact is the overnight run. Optional swap in suggestions.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Reflection beats stay invisible in flow.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -nEi 'sit with|let it land|take a moment|give yourself|breathe|step back|meta-moment|moment of truth' over body -> 0. Closest L74 '## Take stock': the house closing label shared across APT101 exercises, stating artifacts held, not announcing a reflection beat.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No meta-ask when student has already decided.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest apt101-d2-what-ran-overnight 'Ask my first name if you don't know it.' asks for something Claude cannot see, not something already decided. Phases 3 and 5 are person-to-person reads and a team pick; nothing the agent already proposed is re-declared.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: `.md` is default file type for student artifacts across curriculum.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Text artifacts are .md (team/doubts.md). The two .html files (digest-day1.html copy of latest.html, digest-against.html) follow the digest's native format.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cut NVA: true but not moving student forward.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Run NVA before truth. Closest L13 'It takes about five minutes;' changes what the student does (waits for latest.html). L39 'The agent read them once.' sets up the contrast the exercise turns on. L17 tells a student what to do when the run cannot happen. Not obvious to a working engineer; deletion test of L45 loses the typo redirect only.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body "read it" / "look at it" / "notice X" after chat-print = dead weight.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest L39 'Read your own digest.' and L21 'Then read it': the digest is an HTML file the student opens, not a chat print, and both carry follow-on direction (mark the one line you trust least).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forward-callout closer: student as grammatical subject.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest closer L76 'Each of you still knew one source well enough to catch where it went past what was there.' Subject 'Each of you'; declarative, no forward gesture, no role-gating.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Operational reminders live at moment of use, not only where introduced.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Operational setting at moment of use: L7 session/task open with the working folder, L9-11 '/rename apt101-day-2'. Restated here per the rule.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Echo the training's theory spine before inventing a synonym.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest L33/L51 use the training's own frame words (the door, the look-for line, the bet, the headline). No neutral synonym replaces an earned term.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name the artifact, not the act.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -nE 'typing |type in|say to Claude|tell it to' over body -> 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name the outcome; don't walk a professional through trivial mechanics.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest L13 'click Run now on its page': names the one UI control the outcome needs, not a login recipe. grep for flags/env vars/settings.json in body -> 0 (32a).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The curriculum does not narrate itself — subject test, then deletion test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Subject test on orienting sentences: L21 subject 'Each of your agents'/'you'; L74-76 subject 'You'/'the digest'/'Each of you'. No sentence is about a module, the arc or a later beat. grep -nEi 'later|next module|Module [0-9]' over body -> 0 (Day 1 mentions refer to what the student already did).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Exercise headers pass the build-squint test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Header set alone: 'Read the digest' / 'See what ran', 'Mark the line you trust least', 'Read your lines aloud', 'Ask it the other way round', 'Pick the doubt', 'Take stock'. The move is the deliverable (read, doubt, pick), drill carve-out applies and no header is opaque or jargon.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Self-study is invisible in the training flow.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -nEi 'self-study|Teacher Claude' over body -> 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No placeholders inside fences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest 'team/<my-name>/' in the apt101-d2 fences: the training's per-person path template. what-ran-overnight carries the cure at first use ('Ask my first name if you don't know it.'); mark-the-doubt and ask-the-other-way run in the same session after it. mark-the-doubt ends in an open-hook colon where student input is genuinely required (fix d).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every prompt block: one-sentence action lead-in.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L41: lead-in 'Ask Claude to write it down with your reason.' sits before apt101-d2-mark-the-doubt, whose last line is 'The line, and why I trust it least:' (verified: file ends with a colon). This is the rule's mechanical sub-case: a fence ending in a dangling colon awaiting student input, where the lead-in's whole job is naming what to drop in and a summary in front is dead weight. Harm: the one thing not in the fence (what to type after the colon) is not told. Other lead-ins pass: L27 is long (about 75 words, two sentences) against a long multi-step fence, which 2a allows; not filed.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Replace with 'Drop the line after the colon, with your reason.'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Canonical shape — lead-in, label with destination, blank line, fence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Expanded view (expand-md): each fence is lead-in paragraph, blank, '**Prompt** *(Claude Code)*' (or '*(Claude Desktop)*' for personal-agent-homework-3), blank, fence. No 'copy ->' prefix, no end-of-prompt closer. The bare fence at L9-11 is '/rename apt101-day-2', a command, not a prompt block.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Chain by back-reference + deterministic path, never invented alias.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chains carry deterministic paths: Phase 2 appends to team/<my-name>/doubts.md, created by Phase 1's fence; Phase 4 writes team/<my-name>/digest-against.html and reads team/<my-name>/hypothesis.md (Day 1). Closest Phase 2 'Append the line I quote below' anchors to the quoted line in the same fence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Chained-prompt isolation — don't leak downstream pipeline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest Phase 1 fence 'Don't comment on how they compare. That's for us.' points at the team's Phase 3 read without telling Claude what comes next or changing its behavior downstream; it suppresses a second essay.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No session-resets mid-phase.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -ciE '/clear|new session|new conversation' over the four fence files -> 0 each. L7 'Start a new Claude Code session' is the exercise open, not a mid-phase reset.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Markdown shout (`**bold**`, `*italic*`) inside fenced prompts = dead weight in Claude Code.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -cE '\*\*|\*[A-Za-z]' over the four fence files -> 0 each. '## Look for' is the file's heading, plain text.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Citation discipline — extend cite-or-flag scope + quote supporting sentence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Cite-or-flag with quote: what-ran-overnight 'Give each the source file it came from, or "no source"'; mark-the-doubt 'Put the source's own sentence next to the digest's line, both quoted exactly. If the source doesn't say it, say so plainly.' Sentence-level integrity check present.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Overwrite anxiety — name overwrite default on regeneration.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest Phase 4 regeneration: names the destination ('Write the result to team/<my-name>/digest-against.html') and what stays ('Leave morning.md and latest.html untouched'), so no overwrite-or-new pause. Phase 1 copy is to a new path, not a regeneration.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Preamble before action — design around it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Advisory everywhere (own text, 2026-09-08). No permission-mode: plan fence here and no run showed preamble eating a read.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Self-critique register, not defense, when Claude interrogates own work.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Phase 2 fence asks Claude to 'open that source and find what it actually says' and 'say so plainly' if the source doesn't support the line: audit verbs, no defend/justify/prove/argue.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Tell me what you wrote, not show me what you'll write.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Side-effecting fences (file copy, append) report after acting: 'Show me four lines side by side', 'show me its headline beside my first headline'. No irreversible or external action.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Artifact destinations are explicit subpaths, never naked filenames (Agents 101-specific).
rules_evaluated.evidence: Every Save/Write names directory and file: 'team/<my-name>/digest-day1.html', 'team/<my-name>/doubts.md', 'module-2/morning-agent/latest.html', 'team/<my-name>/digest-against.html'. Bare 'morning.md' reads follow the full path given earlier in the same fence; no naked save.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't restate session CWD inside prompt body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -cE '/Users|~/|\bcd ' over the four fence files -> 0 each; paths start from the session root. The body's '~/Documents/apt101/' at L7 is the session-open instruction, outside any fence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name consumer at write time — `Save it as <path>` requires downstream reader.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Consumers named in the maintainer block: digest-day1.html read by Day 3 'what good means'; doubts.md read by Phase 5 and Day 3's caught.md beat; digest-against.html read by Phase 4's comparison and Day 3. Category (b); none is a student-opens-only write.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strong-bold prompt label is exactly `**Prompt**` — custom labels break renderer.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Expanded view: label is exactly '**Prompt**' for all four fences; destination goes in the italic parenthetical.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Normal work request before orchestration.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest what-ran-overnight is a structured multi-move request, but the protocol (copy, four quoted lines, what ran, ranked claims with sources) is the lesson of Phase 1 and starts from the state the body established (the files exist).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Prompts live in registry; module/exercise/lecture files reference by marker.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -c '^\*\*Prompt\*\*' over raw body -> 0 inline blocks; four '{{prompt:<key>}}' markers each on their own line (L15, L29, L43, L62) after a lead-in. Keys resolve to files under curriculum/prompts/.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Module names in prompt prose are fine — they ground the session.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Module names appear only as path segments ('module-2/morning-agent/'), grounding the session; no curricular event cited without an in-session referent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguation, anchors, and decision logic that bind Claude live INSIDE prompt fence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Fences read in isolation run against a realistic state: Phase 1 carries every path it reads and the 'ask my first name' fallback; Phase 4 carries the conditional logic ('If my line looked for support... If my line looked for a test, or looked both ways...') inside the fence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Wide prompts split by logical move — paragraph breaks = cheapest scan-affordance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Phase 1 and Phase 4 fences already scan by move: separate paragraphs for copy, quote-four-lines, what-ran, ranked-claims; bullets for the four lines. Closest ask-the-other-way's two bullets plus 'Either way...' paragraph reads aloud with breaths at the breaks. Condensed-in-a-fence carve-out applies.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body lead-in mirrors prompt's opening phrasing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Phase 1: L27 'keep a copy of the digest... because tonight's run overwrites them' rhymes with the fence's 'First, keep copies before tonight's run overwrites anything.' Phase 4: L60 'run your digest once more from the same brief' rhymes with 'Run the job in morning.md once more, over the same material'. Closest Phase 2: L41 'write it down with your reason' vs 'Append the line I quote below... and my reason' shares the reason clause; the lead-in swap in rule 2 would end on the fence's last line instead, a mismatch the dangling-colon sub-case accepts.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verify session boundary before deciding prompt's context-carrying.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Session boundary read from body: Phase 1 is a fresh session (L7), so its fence carries its own paths; Phases 2 and 4 run in the same session (no /clear between), so back-references to Phase 1 files work. Definite references ('the line I quote below', 'my first headline') resolve in scrollback.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Artifact-vs-STOP tail ordering — last imperative wins.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest Phase 4 tail: 'Write the result to team/<my-name>/digest-against.html. Then show me its headline beside my first headline, both quoted exactly. Add nothing.' The write is not blocked; 'Add nothing' scopes to the display.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Long-running prompts stream progress — never go silent.
